pull_requests.title: feat: TRT-LLM DeepSeek-V4 collectors — mHC + CSA/HCA attention modules (#1480)
pull_requests.body:
**Scope** (clarified per review, 2026-08-19): #1480 asks for mHC on `1.3.0rc20 (and future versions)` across all eight trtllm systems, and for full DSV4 modeling. This PR delivers (a) the **mHC module tables at rc20 on all eight systems** — the issue's original ask in full — and (b) the **DSV4 attention family at rc23 on the four Blackwell systems**, which is the framework's entire DSV4 support surface: the model class and sparse backend first ship in 1.3.0rc21, and the framework hard-rejects pre-Blackwell GPUs (mla.py `forward_*_sparse_mla`) — an rc20/eight-system DSV4 attention collection is not physically possible. #1480 is updated accordingly.

**DeepSeek-V4 on trtllm now models end-to-end on all four Blackwell systems** — `aiconfigurator cli default` produces agg+disagg Pareto configurations for DSV4 Flash/Pro on b200_sxm, b300_sxm, gb200 and gb300.

## What's in this PR (by commit group)

**Collectors**
- `collect_mhc_module.py`: mHC pre/post module tables (trtllm≥1.3.0rc20). AutoTuner serving-parity warmup; per-row observed `kernel_source` (fma / dg_splitk / dg_nosplit). Validated on H20; collected on all 8 trtllm systems (1101 rows).
- `collect_dsv4_attn.py`: the four DSV4 CSA/HCA context/generation module tables (trtllm≥1.3.0rc21; framework rejects pre-Blackwell inside the module forward — mla.py `forward_*_sparse_mla` @rc23). Framework-dispatch construction (`from_pretrained` auto-builds the deepseek_v4 sparse config; CSA/HCA via `compress_ratios=[4|128]`); KVCacheManagerV2 with explicit byte quota; engine-envelope `max_seq_len` with real per-request KV state; #1429 row semantics (rank-local heads + tp_size). Five B200 smoke rounds → 44/48, 0 bad rows.
- Size-1 module cache across same-geometry cases (75f888f5): A/B'd 44/44 vs the uncached collector (median 1.002) — and it *fixed* a measurement artifact: long-lived modules are what serving runs, and cold-module collection inflated long-prefix CSA context outliers (497ms → 37.2ms warm ≈ vllm's 39ms).
- Registry: SM120 parked with hardware probe evidence (RTX PRO 6000: 100% classified failures, DeepGEMM family limit). Pre-Blackwell fails classified by framework design — trtllm's DSV4 support surface is b200/b300/gb200/gb300, narrower than sglang/vllm (which cover SM90).
- Manifest: `trtllm.families.sparse_attention → 1.3.0rc23` (per-family override; DSA smoke-verified on rc23/SM90 for the drag-along).

**Mechanism (owner decision, tianhaox 2026-08-08)**
- `derive_table_status`: a table is `partial` only on a ModuleCollectionFailure. **Recorded per-case failures are DATA** (failure_handling.md doctrine) — deterministic framework limits (sweep-extreme OOM, the 262144-query-token launch cluster, platform rejections) land in the classified log without making the campaign unpublishable. Anti-false-success is unchanged: dying runs never finalize (missing-sidecar coverage gate), zero-row ops still demote. Design doc §5 updated.

**Data** (all content-verified through the unchanged aic-core loaders)
- mHC: 8 systems × trtllm/1.3.0rc20 (b300/gb300 140/140; b200/gb200/h200 139; h100 136; rtx_pro 136; l40s 132 — failures are top-of-sweep OOM matching VRAM; SM89/SM120 run FMA-only, SM90/100/103 add DeepGEMM TF32 tactics).
- DSV4 modules: **all four Blackwell systems × trtllm/1.3.0rc23, collected with the warm-module collector at one ref (75f888f5)**. Generation tables are full-grid (1544/1544, zero failures — the engine-envelope floor removed the tiny-KV HCA assert cluster). Context tables carry the parked kernel-limit clusters as recorded failures (~240/table: 262144-query-token launch limit + small OOM tail; 5584–5600 of 5840 measured). gb200/gb300 tables **replace** the earlier cold-module collection; b200/b300 are new, collected via per-table split pipelines after the combined runs exhausted computelab window budgets. First-wins dedup collapses cross-window resume re-measurements; `rows` in every sidecar now matches the shipped parquet.
- Cross-system parity (same-shape latency medians): b300/b200 ≈ 0.96, b200/gb200 ≈ 1.03–1.06, b300/gb300 ≈ 1.02–1.04 — consistent with the 1000W (SXM) vs 1200W (NVL) power envelopes. One known single-point outlier: gb200 csa_context (Flash, bs1, isl4, prefix2048) reads 1.83ms where b200 reads 0.15ms — interpolation smooths it; flagged for spot re-measurement.
- `reuse.yaml` (4 Blackwell systems × mhc/gemm/moe/comm/quantize): rc23 reuses the rc20 shared layer, approved_by tianhaox; rc20→rc23 validity rides the standard upgrade audit.
- Meta statuses derived from the runs' own checkpoints; synthesized sidecar entries (tables finalized host-side from `--keep-csv` staging) reuse the sibling `collector_hash` at the shared ref and a checkpoint- or generator-derived `case_plan_hash` (generator hashing validated bit-exact against a checkpoint-derived hash before use).

## End-to-end evidence (SILICON mode, 8 GPU, isl4096/osl1024, TTFT 2000ms / TPOT 50ms)

| system × model | backend | agg tokens/s/gpu | best parallel |
|---|---|---|---|
| gb200 × Flash-FP8 | **trtllm 1.3.0rc23** | **4828.8** | dp4 ep4, bs240 |
| b200 × Flash-FP8 | **trtllm 1.3.0rc23** | **4562.5** | dp4 ep4, bs224 |
| gb200 × Flash-FP8 | sglang 0.5.14 | 3343.3 | dp4 etp4, bs160 |
| gb200 × Flash-FP8 | vllm 0.24.0 | 2555.9 | dp4 etp4, bs128 |
| gb300 × Pro-FP8 | **trtllm 1.3.0rc23** | **552.0** | dp8 ep8, bs28 |
| b300 × Pro-FP8 | **trtllm 1.3.0rc23** | **278.6** | tp8 ep8, bs112 |
| gb300 × Pro-FP8 | sglang 0.5.14 | 317.4 | dp8 etp2ep4, bs16 |
| gb300 × Pro-FP8 | vllm 0.24.0 | 127.8 | tp8 (likely coverage-limited) |

b300 × Pro lands at half of gb300 for a mechanical reason: Pro's weights fit replicated (dp8) in gb300's HBM but not in b300's, so the optimizer falls back to tp8 sharding — a capacity effect, not a kernel gap (kernel medians are ~parity, see above).

Cross-framework op-level parity was audited separately (B200, exact-key joins): post-attention identical across engines; trtllm CSA/HCA prefill mostly faster; trtllm CSA decode 1.3–2× slower at tiny shapes (default-off cute-DSL/heuristic-topk paths — the collector logs the resolved knobs per build). The previously-reported 12.7× CSA long-prefix outlier was a **cold-module collection artifact, not serving behavior** — warm-module re-collection brings it to 37.2ms ≈ vllm's 39ms (audit conclusion amended; all four systems shipped warm).

## Review response (Arsene12358, 2026-08-19 — six blocking items)

1. **moe rc23 plan hashes**: real bug (offline sidecar authoring hashed an empty case set). Regenerated all four `case_plan_hash` values from the campaign checkpoints' `done ∪ failed` ids (231 attempted cases; artifact rows verified identical to the committed parquet). Added collector-data rule **R7 "attested case plan"** — a sidecar entry with `rows > 0` and the empty-plan hash now fails the gate — with unit tests.

pull_requests.title: fix(aic-core): DSV4 CSA CP parity — mHC seq_split, reuse-aware top_last, mixed-pass filters (Phase 2 PR-2.5)
pull_requests.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Rebased onto `main`** (`9eda26c9`, 2026-08-13 — twice: first over #1461/#1447/#1503/#1514, then over #1479/#1511): the mHC `seq_split` schema bump renumbers to **v10** (main claimed v7–v9), and the goldens were recaptured from the rebased tree (diff vs main's goldens: the DSV4 CP case/surfaces added, ~112 metrics at <1e-12 fold-order noise, zero error flips). The review's handle-cache correctness blocker is fixed on top (`database_policy` in the cache identity) with key-level + behavioral regression tests, the live-Python run_mixed regression test, and the README/docstring refreshes.

## What

Phase 2 PR-2.5. Fixes #1498 — both defects, adjudicated piecewise as the issue prescribed — plus two more one-sided behaviors the investigation unearthed, which belong to the same PR-2 error-symmetry scope.

### 1. The 34% CP composition divergence: rust mHC was missing the CP token division
The adjudication exonerated the issue's suspects — the CP attention composition (`_query_cp` vs `query_cp_with`, incl. all AG terms and the per-card base) agrees **bit-exact** (16.520287 ms both engines). The entire 14.51 ms delta was `context_mhc_pre/post`: Python's `DeepSeekV4MHCModule` is `_CP_AWARE` (queries at `ceil(x/seq_split)`), while rust's `MhcModuleOp` had no `seq_split` field and the opspec never carried it — the compiled engine queried the mHC table at the full 8192 tokens (43 × mhc(8192) = 9.563/7.955 ms vs Python's 43 × mhc(1024) = 1.849/1.157 ms; numeric closure exact). A sweep confirmed mHC was the **only** op receiving `seq_split=cp` without a rust-side field (MoE omits it deliberately — CP-invariant).

Fix: `seq_split` on `MhcModuleOp` (serde default 1, `div_ceil` at query entry — before the SOL/silicon/empirical dispatch, exactly where Python divides), serialized by `engine.py`; `ENGINE_SPEC_SCHEMA_VERSION` 9 → 10 both sides (op-payload layout change, same precedent as v5; originally claimed 7, renumbered at the 2026-08-13 rebase after main's v7–v9 landings). Rust oracle pins pre/post/both at the shard count, ceil rounding, and the `seq_split=1` identity against Python-generated values.

**After: both engines report 42.430756 ms at the repro shape.**

### 2. Reuse-aware CP top_last loader on both engines (defect 1)
`_load_csa_topk_top_last` now projects the same `_build_op_sources` + `load_dsv4_sparse_op_data` resolution as its DELTA sibling, so approved `reuse.yaml` donors serve the CP rows too. The rust loader's PRIMARY-source-only gate (added by #1496 solely to mirror the pre-fix Python error surface) is removed in the same change — both grids consume the full ordered source list (first-wins; rows lacking `num_heads` skipped, per the shared generic loader's missing-key-cell contract). Anchored by rust donor/no-column loader tests and Python pins on the shipped `b200_sxm/sglang/0.5.12` donor grid. DeepSeek-V4-Flash tp1 ep8 cp8 static_ctx now computes **42.430756 ms on both engines on both 0.5.12 (donor) and 0.5.14 (primary)**.

### 3. `run_mixed` passes query only the ops they consume
Unearthed while anchoring the mixed surface: Python's three mixed-step passes ran the FULL op lists through `run_static` and discarded everything but the consumed bucket, so a raise in a discarded query blocked the estimate on the Python side only — the rust mixed step has always walked exactly the consumed sets (`ContextOpFilter::{Skip,Only}ContextAttention` / `only_generation_attention`). Concrete instance: the DSV4 CP case's pass 3 hit the generation-MoE singleton low-token miss and raised while the compiled engine computed (static_gen errors symmetrically, so the gap was confined to the mixed orchestration). `_run_context_phase` / `_run_generation_phase` gain an op-name filter and the passes call them directly. Consumed values untouched: key-exact golden comparison shows **zero error-class flips** and only ~3e-16 fold-order noise; the DSV4 mixed surface now computes **46.0492671363915 ms bit-identically on both engines**.

### 4. `run_mixed` pass-1 prefix kept integral
`np.floor` yielded a float64 prefix that contaminated the ops' `s = isl - prefix`; the DSV4 CP composition's chunk decomposition (`range()` over `s`) was the first strict-int consumer to crash on it. The product is integral, so `int()` is lossless — also previously unreachable (the CP path raised first, defect 1).

### Parity anchors
- New `cp_static_ctx` surface (`cli_estimate` has no cp knob, so the "static" surface cannot express CP) + `DSV4_CP_CASES` pinning the adjudicated repro on the reuse-carrying 0.5.12, on BOTH `cp_static_ctx` and `mixed` surfaces.
- Goldens recaptured from clean trees at each anchor commit; capture verified byte-idempotent.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Adjudicated repro (b200_sxm/sglang/0.5.14, DSV4-Flash tp1 ep8 cp8, static_ctx) | python == rust == 42.430756 ms (was 42.43 vs 56.94) |
| Same on reuse-dependent 0.5.12 (donor) | identical, both engines (was: both raise) |
| Mixed surface, same config | python == rust == 46.0492671363915 ms (was: python raise, rust 46.05) |
| cargo test --release (lib) | 421 passed (rebased tree) |
| Python unit suite | 3480 passed / 50 skipped (rebased tree, incl. the new policy/regression tests) |
| engine-step + compile-engine parity | 447 passed (rebased tree, incl. main's FPM parity + the handle-policy isolation tests) |
| Golden impact of the pass-filter change | 0 error flips, ~112 metrics at <1e-12 (fold order) on the rebased base, 1 new case |
| ruff check / ruff format / cargo fmt | clean |

## Notes for reviewers
- The mHC field addition bumps `ENGINE_SPEC_SCHEMA_VERSION` (9 → 10 after the rebase renumber); the public-api contract pin is updated in the same commit.
- The former one-sided scan DRIFTs (#1496's "9 CSA CP entries") should now compute on both engines; a full support-matrix rerun is planned post-rebase.
- `csa_topk_top_last_raw_rows_lookup` was rewritten for the new loader contract: rows without `num_heads` never load (previously the no-column fixture resolved at any head count) — this matches the DELTA pairing's existing requirement and #1429's mandatory-column convention.

pull_requests.body:
## 功能概述

本 PR 为 DSV4 Flash 增加独立的 MegaKernel decode 路径，重点优化 Attention sublayer；prefill 和不满足 MegaKernel 约束的请求继续使用原有实现。此 PR 仅涉及框架层适配，无算子变更

## Mega Attention

- 在 `Block.forward_decode` 接入完整 sublayer adapter：compress ratio 为 4 的层选择 CSA，compress ratio 为 128 的层选择 HCA。adapter 统一编排 Hyper-Connection、RMSNorm、Q 投影与量化、RoPE、Attention、输出投影和 residual 回写，避免框架侧重复拆分和中间结果搬运。
- CSA 路径保留 indexer/TopK 和稀疏 Attention 语义；HCA 路径按其无 indexer/TopK 的几何使用专用 front、Q-B、RMSNorm/RoPE 链路。两条路径直接复用 RTP-LLM 的 FP8 KV cache、slot mapping、decode metadata 和原生 FlashMLA，不改变上层请求及 cache 管理协议。
- 模型初始化阶段将 checkpoint 权重打包为 CUDA 算子要求的 fused layout，并根据 DSV4 Pro/Flash geometry 选择对应实现。模型级 runtime 跨层管理 workspace、RoPE table 和 MQA schedule，保持 CUDA Graph capture/replay 使用的 tensor 地址稳定。
- 支持常规单 token decode，以及 DSpARK draft、MTP target verify 等 multi-token decode。当前在 FP8 KV、TP1 且 `B*S <= 128` 时默认启用；单次请求形状不满足约束时回退原 Attention 路径，也可通过 `DSV4_MEGA_CSA=0`、`DSV4_MEGA_HCA=0` 分别关闭。

## MoE

Mega decode 的 MoE 前端使用 CUDA extension 融合 Hyper-Connection、RMSNorm、router/quant/post/comb 和 TopK。前端输出继续进入框架默认的 MegaMoE-SE；普通路径仍使用原有 HC/norm/router/pack 链路，并与 Mega 路径共用同一个 MegaMoE-SE 后端。

pull_requests.title: Fix NVRTC compilation for HyperConnection kernels
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Include `<cuda_device_runtime_api.h>` in the SM90 and SM100 HyperConnection pre-norm GEMM kernels.
- Make the `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` declaration available to the NVRTC compilation path.

## Root cause

Both HyperConnection kernels call the Programmatic Dependent Launch synchronization intrinsic. With `DG_JIT_USE_NVRTC=1`, the current include chain does not expose its device-runtime declaration, so NVRTC fails with:

```text
identifier "cudaGridDependencySynchronize" is undefined
```

NVCC provides the declaration implicitly in this path, which is why the failure is NVRTC-specific.

## Impact

This restores NVRTC compilation for both SM90 and SM100 HyperConnection kernels. It does not change kernel logic, synchronization behavior, or launch configuration.

## Validation

- CUDA 12.9.1 NVRTC compile-only regression:
  - [Before the fix](https://github.com/nya-a-cat/DeepGEMM/actions/runs/29105589876): SM90 compilation fails with the undefined identifier above.
  - [After the fix](https://github.com/nya-a-cat/DeepGEMM/actions/runs/29108998119): the SM90 and SM100 header instantiations compile successfully.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`

GPU runtime validation was not performed because the Actions runner did not have an NVIDIA GPU.

Fixes #359

## 🤖 ds-review-bot Code Review

### v4
The patch re-enables NVRTC (DG_JIT_USE_NVRTC=1) compilation of the SM90/SM100 HyperConnection pre-norm GEMM kernels by adding `#include <cuda_device_runtime_api.h>` to both kernel headers, which exposes the `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` PDL device-runtime declaration that NVCC supplies implicitly but NVRTC does not. It is minimal, touches only the two affected files, and by inspection does not change kernel logic/sync/launch. The main concern is that the include is placed unconditionally at file scope, outside the device/`__CUDACC_RTC__`/`__CLION_IDE__` guard that surrounds the actual PDL call and the rest of the kernel body; the same .cuh is also parsed by the host/prebuilt/NVCC/clang-cuda compilation paths (through indexing/main.cu and the JIT pipeline), which neither need nor generally expect a device-runtime-only toolkit header. The patch was validated only via NVRTC compile-only regressions, so the effect on those other compiler configurations is unverified. Recommendation: guard/place the include consistently (or use a `__CUDACC_RTC__`-guarded minimal prototype) and re-run a full build (NVCC/clang/prebuilt) plus a GPU run before merge.

### v3
This PR adds `#include <cuda_device_runtime_api.h>` to the two HyperConnection TF32 pre-norm GEMM kernels (sm90_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm.cuh:5 and sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm.cuh:5) so that the `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` intrinsic declaration is available on the NVRTC compilation path (DG_JIT_USE_NVRTC=1). The change is correct and minimal: both kernels call cudaGridDependencySynchronize() (sm90 line 122, sm100 line 139), an intrinsic declared in <cuda_device_runtime_api.h> that NVCC pulls in implicitly but NVRTC does not, causing the reported 'identifier cudaGridDependencySynchronize is undefined' failure. This update introduces new kernels, features, and performance improvements:

### New kernels
  - Sparse Indexer: hierarchical sparse indexing for V4.1, with throughput close to the Lightning Indexer.
  - Mega Gate: fuses the routing GEMM and multiple MoE routing operations into one kernel, with 30–75% speedups.
  - Mega mHC: fuses multiple Hyper-Connection operations and RMSNorm into one kernel, with 45–85% speedups.

### New features
  - Integration with [DeepJIT](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepJIT), a lightweight, header-only JIT runtime.
  - More epilogue fusion options, including runtime alpha scaling and fused output casting.
  - Broader use of cuBLASLt for simpler GEMM and batched operations.

### Performance improvements
  - Faster MoE backward GEMMs, with ~20% gains.
  - Mega MoE optimizations for V4.1: ~15% faster at low latency, ~4% at high throughput.
  - Improved Lightning Indexer kernels, with a follow-up version (~30% faster) coming soon.

### Breaking changes
  - Previously, all kernels were fully deterministic and batch-invariant.
  - This release adds a `use_deterministic_algorithms()` API, which defaults to `False` so some kernels can run faster.
  - Set it to `True` to restore deterministic, batch-invariant behavior for RL and similar workloads.

pull_requests.title: fix(mhc): MHCPreNormFn.backward returns wrong number of gradients
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

`MHCPreNormFn.forward` (`tile_kernels/modeling/mhc/ops/norm_fn.py`) takes **5** user inputs (`x`, `fn`, `norm_eps`, `fuse_grad_acc`, `n_splits`), but `backward` returns **6** elements. PyTorch autograd requires one returned gradient per input, so this raises at runtime:

```
RuntimeError: function MHCPreNormFnBackward returned an incorrect number of gradients (expected 5, got 6)
```

## Fix

Drop the trailing `None` from both return statements so the arity matches the 5 forward inputs, and update the type annotation to reflect the real return shape (`x_grad` is `None` when `fuse_grad_acc=True`).

```diff
-    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, None, None]:
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor | None, torch.Tensor, None, None, None]:
...
-            return None, fn_grad, None, None, None, None
-        return x_grad, fn_grad, None, None, None, None
+            return None, fn_grad, None, None, None
+        return x_grad, fn_grad, None, None, None
```

pull_requests.body:
## 📌 Description

Hopper-targeted optimization of the `mhc_pre_big_fuse` kernel. The change is gated
behind `#if __CUDA_ARCH__ == 900`, so **all non-Hopper architectures compile the
original code path unchanged** — only `sm_90` (H100) takes the new path, which is
the only GPU it has been profiled on.

Two micro-architectural changes to the per-token metadata stage (the warp-0 work
that produces `pre_mix`/`post_mix`/`comb_mix`):

1. **Remove a 96-byte local-memory spill.** The mix vector was held in a
   `float y_local[24]` indexed by the runtime `lane`, which ptxas placed in local
   memory (`STACK:96`, confirmed via `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage`). Each active
   lane now loads only its own 6-element slice into scalar / constant-indexed
   registers → `STACK:0`, `LOCAL:0`.
2. **Overlap the Sinkhorn projection with the reduction.** `pre_mix` (the only
   coefficient the `layer_input` reduction consumes) is published *before* the block
   barrier. The 20-iteration Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization that produces `comb_mix`
   on warp 0 now runs concurrently with the bandwidth-bound reduction on warps 1+,
   instead of serializing in front of it.

Numerics are unchanged (identical ops and ordering); the existing reference tests
pass within tolerance. The portable path is byte-for-byte the original kernel.


`mhc_post` is not modified by this PR; measured original-vs-this-branch latency is
within ±1% (run-to-run noise) across the full sweep, confirming no regression.
Sub-µs differences at very small M/S are likewise within noise.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up perf work on the mHC kernels from #3285 (DeepSeek-V4 issue #3346).

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [✅] `pre-commit run --files csrc/mhc/mhc_pre_big_fuse.cu` — `clang-format`, tabs and
  CRLF hooks all pass (no reformatting required).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Existing reference tests pass unchanged on H100:

```bash
  pytest -q tests/mhc/test_mhc_post.py
  pytest -q tests/mhc/test_mhc_pre_big_fuse.py   # 26 passed
```

```bash
  python benchmarks/bench_mhc_pre_big_fuse.py
  python benchmarks/bench_mhc_post.py
```

## Reviewer Notes

- The optimization is **strictly `__CUDA_ARCH__ == 900`**; `sm_80`/`sm_100`/etc. are
  untouched. If reviewers prefer it enabled on other archs, the guard is a one-line
  change once those targets are profiled.
- Profiled on an H100 via Modal. Nsight Compute hardware counters are unavailable in
  that sandbox (`LibraryNotLoaded`), so the analysis used measured latency,
  derived HBM-bandwidth (algorithmic bytes / latency vs the 3.35 TB/s roofline), and
  `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage` for the register/spill evidence. On the `pure`
  (BigFuse) path the change lifts large-`N` HBM utilization from ~67–78% to ~88–90%.
- The `prenorm` path still makes two streaming passes over `residual` (sqrsum, then
  the weighted-sum reduction); a single-pass shared-memory fusion is a natural
  follow-up but is left out here to keep the change small and `sm_90`-scoped.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a Hopper (sm_90) fast path in the `mhc_pre_big_fuse_kernel` to optimize register usage and overlap the Sinkhorn projection with the layer input reduction. The review feedback suggests optimizing performance by replacing division operations with reciprocal multiplication inside the loops where `row_sum` is a common denominator.

csrc/mhc/mhc_pre_big_fuse.cu (2)
`280-280`: _⚡ Quick win_ **Document the deadlock-free invariant the overlap depends on.** The whole overlap is safe only because warp 0 (the Sinkhorn producer) skips `write_layer_input` via its early return (Line 172), and `write_layer_input` contains no block-wide `__syncthreads()`. If a future change adds any block barrier inside `write_layer_input`, warps 1+ would block on a barrier warp 0 never reaches — a hard-to-diagnose deadlock that only manifests on sm_90. A short comment at this barrier (and/or near `write_layer_input`) recording this contract is cheap insurance for a concurrency-critical path.

In `@csrc/mhc/mhc_pre_big_fuse.cu` at line 280, This synchronization depends on the invariant that the Sinkhorn producer (warp 0) may early-return and thus skip calling write_layer_input, so write_layer_input must not contain any block-wide barrier (e.g., __syncthreads()) or any code that could cause some warps to block while warp 0 continues; add a concise comment at this __syncthreads() and directly above the write_layer_input declaration noting: "Contract: write_layer_input must be free of block-level barriers or any warp-divergent blocking calls because warp 0 may early-return and not reach those barriers; if you need synchronization, make it warp-local or ensure all warps execute the same path." ## 📌 Description

  Reference implementation of the `flashinfer.experimental` proposal: an isolated,
  minimally-reviewed landing zone for consumer-GPU (SM12x) kernels, fenced off so it can
  never affect datacenter users — plus the first corpus to live in it.

  **What's inside** — `flashinfer.experimental.sm12x`, a curated port of the b12x
  CuTe-DSL kernel corpus (`lukealonso/b12x @ 6627d342`, CUTLASS DSL 4.6): 15 ops in 6 groups.

  | Group | Ops |
  |---|---|
  | `attention` | `paged` (decode/extend, FP8 KV, MSA block-sparse), `sparse_mla` (DSV4/GLM top-k  MLA + NVFP4 FP8-RoPE cache writer), `compressed_mla`, `nsa_indexer`, `varlen` |
  | `gemm` | `blockscaled` (NVFP4/MXFP4/MXFP8), `block_fp8_linear`, `mxfp8_linear`,
  `wo_projection` |
  | `moe` | `fused_moe` (nvfp4/mxfp4/w4a8/w4a16 + NF3 layouts), `ep_moe` |
  | `norm` / `quantization` / `comm` | `mhc`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, `pcie` (PCIe collectives) |

  **Proposal rules, enforced by blocking CI lints rather than convention:**

  - **Isolation**: zero outbound imports (experimental never imports core; capability gating
    is vendored) and core never imports experimental — which also structurally proves
    `aot.py` / jit-cache / cubin wheels can never pick up experimental code.
  - **Arch restriction**: no SM90/SM100/SM103/SM110 targets anywhere in the tree.
  - **Side-effect-free namespace**: `import flashinfer.experimental.sm12x` pulls no
    cutlass/triton, registers no torch ops, and emits exactly one `FutureWarning`
    (`FLASHINFER_EXP_QUIET=1` silences). Kernels load on first op use.
  - **JIT only**: pure Python + JIT sources (raw `.cu` only inside `comm/pcie/`,
    registered as package-data per the existing `cute_dsl/sparse/blk64` precedent).

  **One grammar**: every op declares itself via a `META` header (entry points, dtypes,
  requirements, provenance, test path; `sm12x.list_ops()` enumerates), and stateful ops
  share one serving-grade lifecycle — `plan()` may allocate, `bind()` builds views only
  (never allocates), `run*()` is CUDA-graph-capture safe — with serving freeze controls
  at the arch root. See `flashinfer/experimental/README.md` for the full contract and
  the b12x → experimental migration map.

  **Core-facing footprint** (the part that needs real review, all in the first commit):
  mypy/pre-commit/ruff excludes for the experimental subtree, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` floor
  `4.5.0 → 4.5.2` (experimental additionally runtime-gates itself at `>= 4.6.0` without
  constraining core installs), one package-data entry, and one new non-blocking CI
  workflow. Wheel grows ~1–1.5 MB compressed. Core code paths are untouched.

  ## 🔍 Related Issues

  <!-- TODO: link the flashinfer.experimental proposal / RFC discussion -->

  ## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

  ### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

  - [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred  method).
  - [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
  - [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported
  issues.

  ## 🧪 Tests

  - [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
  - [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

  `tests/experimental/`: 127 tests — structural lints (blocking, stdlib-only), subprocess
  import-hygiene, registry contract, and curated small-shape kernel tests (pure-torch
  references, flashinfer-core cuDNN `mm_fp4` oracle bitwise parity, CUDA-graph replays
  under frozen kernel resolution). All green on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) with
  `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.0`; dense NVFP4 GEMM verified bitwise-identical to upstream
  b12x with perf ratio 1.000. GPU CI is templated but disabled until an SM12x runner
  exists — until then the GPU lane is a local runbook.

  ## Reviewer Notes

  - **Review model** (per the proposal): commit 1 (`experimental: scaffold …`) is the
    line-review target — namespace, rules, lints, CI, and the config edits. Commits 2–6
    are mechanical kernel drops whose review is "the lints are green, the tests exist and
    passed on SM120, provenance headers are present"; every ported file carries its
    upstream path + commit, and each op's `META.provenance` pins the source revision.
  - `torch.ops.flashinfer_sm12x.*` is a **private** integration namespace
    (torch.compile/graph tracing only); the documented Python API is the surface.
  - Known caveats are declared in-tree, not hidden: `attention.paged` decode graph replay
    is implemented but currently untested in-tree (upstream's replay tests are stale;
    noted in `META.notes`), and `attention.varlen` is marked reduced-assurance.
  - Pre-commit: `pre-commit run --all-files` is green. The four ported `.cu` files are
    excluded from clang-format (kept byte-faithful to upstream, matching the subtree's
    mypy/ruff exemptions); this change also repairs the hook's exclude regex, which was
    silently matching nothing (`(?x)` verbose mode ate the separator).

pull_requests.body:
**Draft — correctness validation is recorded below; sparse and varlen performance follow-ups remain open.**

Bring the SGL DeepGEMM fork to upstream’s September release while retaining the SGL wheel, TVM FFI interface, and downstream kernels. This is a two-parent merge of upstream `66081d4c9c7d7c44f13fea402e5b622aa0f409c2` (Public Release 26/09, deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#432) into `origin/dev` at `60651a75d1e8742633982c8124f36abcbcaff8e0`.

**Merge this PR with a merge commit to preserve the upstream ancestry.**

### Features, compatibility, and packaging

- Adopt DeepJIT and upstream MegaGate, MegaMHC, scheduled/sparse MQA, quantized einsum output, GEMM alpha epilogues, K-grouped FP4, cuBLASLt NVFP4, and batched symmetric operations. Preserve existing public positional prefixes and defaults while exposing new options through the SGL wrappers.
- Retain Hopper and SM120 dispatch, NVFP4/MXFP4, SiTU/SwiGLU-OAI, pre-dispatch, FP8 combine, and per-layer/per-expert scaling. MegaMoE intermediates above 4096 use a scalable readiness protocol; the existing smaller-shape fast path remains.
- Preserve legacy K-grouped alignments, partial K tiles, empty groups, compact scales, and `ks` host-list/`None`/empty-list forms. The appended `use_padded_sf_layout=False` keeps packed-scale callers compatible; `True` opts into upstream’s padded layout. Standalone scale packing remains available on H200. FP4 granularity-128 recipes retain the expanded MMA path, while eligible granularity-32 inputs use native FP4.
- Mirror all 12 changed upstream `tests/` files (10 test modules and two helpers) into `sgl_deep_gemm/tests/`, preserving assertions and parameter coverage. Keep the downstream MegaMoE suite as `test_mega_moe_sgl.py` alongside upstream shared-expert/FP8×FP8 coverage. Retain Hopper, SiTU, NVFP4, tiny-decode, pre-dispatch, and legacy tests; fix reference imports, child-failure propagation, and sanitizer discovery.
- Package DeepJIT headers in the SGL wheel and replace the old JIT/fmt integration. The Ubuntu 22.04 release workflow installs and selects GCC/G++ 13 plus `libdw-dev` for C++20/DeepJIT, preserving its glibc baseline. Pin the test reference dependencies to compatible TileLang/TileKernels versions.

### Correctness fixes exposed by integration and hardware validation

- Preserve caller-owned MegaGate output tensors across the FFI boundary, preventing allocator reuse after a temporary output dictionary is released. Preserve backing-storage capacity for padded/offset mHC scale views and reject invalid workspace requests before allocating scratch.
- Reset mHC’s active barrier region and MegaMoE’s peer-ready tags in stream/barrier order. CUDA graph replay can reuse grid IDs, so old terminal tags must not satisfy a later replay. Permanent regressions change inputs at captured addresses and retain the original references and tolerances.
- Restore FP8 and packed-byte activation dtypes after importing MegaMoE symmetric-buffer views through DLPack. This prevents numeric conversion into signed bytes from corrupting FP8 inputs. Match FP4 pre-dispatch midpoint rounding to the upstream ties-to-even helper.
- Clamp both cleanup endpoints to logical KV length, including bulk and scalar passes, and run SM120 cleanup after compute. These preserve masks for nonaligned, empty, and out-of-range query intervals.
- Bound contiguous sparse KV/SF tail copies by the physical allocation, keeping full-block copies and paged addressing intact. The permanent regression checks 104 exact-allocation cases with hand-derived outputs. Rematerialize the sparse MXFP8 math warp index after register allocation to eliminate the observed spills.

### Scoped performance and compiler changes

SM100 prefers non-overlapping TMEM layouts only for validated large batched FP8 projections and mixed FP8×FP4 FP32-accumulation shapes. Original admissibility checks and explicit block-size constraints still apply; an empty preferred subset falls back to the original candidates.

Dense MQA uses separate cleanup and full-span unrolling only in measured long-query families. The compressed MXFP8 fence adjustment retains all TMEM fences, waits, and Q-stage reuse ordering. Scoped CTA-index lifetimes and register budgets removed the initially observed spills; the original 1,180-template sample passed. The full enumeration exposed an additional unrolled H8/D128 template with an 8-byte spill. A guarded row-index identity now removes that spill while preserving the original 56/224 dynamic register allocation and all synchronization. The NVFP4 I8192 dispatch fix similarly localizes its ready-counter index before the unchanged release-add. A fixed next-N=6 paged BF16 family uses a wide TMEM load, with all completion waits retained; the audited affected kernels are identical to the versions validated on hardware. Hopper uses limited register/unroll changes and default-mode N specialization, honoring compile-dimension overrides and existing tile choices. Narrow Gate/mHC compiler overrides retain strict spill checking.

Controlled measurements use identical encoded inputs on the same physical GPU and time the full operation, including auxiliary kernels. Representative results:

- The batched FP8 einsum regression returns near baseline latency; mixed FP8×FP4 improves about 5.6% versus the initial merged selection, retaining approximately 1.2% latency overhead versus `dev`.
- The fixed paged FP8 case with batch 256, next-N 6, page size 64, 64 heads, head dimension 32 and KV length 65536 returns from 616.5 to 585.8 µs (baseline 586.1 µs). Six affected cases pass three alternating baseline/merged/fixed comparisons; short-KV full-operation residuals remain 1–2.2%.
- The long H64 MQA cleanup cases return within 1% of baseline across paired graph measurements. Residual MQA costs remain: roughly 2.1–2.2% for one legacy FP32 family and 2–4% for some short-KV/below-threshold H64 controls. Selected spill-free mHC compiler configurations also retain approximately 2.8% graph overhead.
- Hopper’s 42-case normal FP8 comparison ranges from −2.38% to +86.86% throughput versus baseline. Two-rank FP8 MegaMoE preserves the standard shared-expert case (~+0.15% throughput) and improves the small case (~+22%); both arms use the same activation-view correction and identical quantized operands.

### Validation status

The original merge commit is `49018416`; follow-up sparse fix `b80f3b7` and dense/NVFP4 spill fix `89dcf42` preserve that merge history. The current tree is `3f2060acc5bb047d957d80449ba40e0a62d39fbd`. Its rebuilt B200 wheel has SHA256 `ed4b8e8d6783e30c800500394727eb9b4b0467c0a27fce85a84c1eda5761751e`; all 220 source entries and 921 installed wheel members were verified. The combined wheel passes all48 dense packet case executions and all three original two-rank BF16/NVFP4 test invocations. Its actual generated GPU executable sections match the corresponding previously validated private fixes. All8461 environment files and native/reference dependencies remained unchanged. The earlier sparse wheel/tree remains independently archived, as do earlier component source and binary records.

| Coverage | Current result |
|---|---|
| H200 applicable functional coverage | Passed, including 61 multi-layer accuracy cases and final rebuilt-wheel Hopper/lazy/pre-dispatch checks |
| H200 memcheck/synccheck | 48 applicable function/tool pairs covered; 10 architecture-only cases are N/A. Four earlier spill failures have final-wheel full-function passing replacements |
| B200 core module mains | All nine passed: BF16, FP8/FP4, einsum, hyperconnection, layout, legacy, MegaGate, mHC, and cleanup bounds |
| B200 multi-GPU/MoE/lazy coverage | Ten invocations passed, including standard 4-rank suites, 24 BF16 graph replays, and supplemental FP8×FP8 coverage |
| Final paged kernel changes | Six canonical cases × memcheck/synccheck plus cached graph checks passed; four additional checks passed on the rebuilt wheel |
| Remaining Blackwell sanitizer coverage | All 52 original nonattention function/tool pairs passed, including all 588 K-grouped memcheck variants (462 FP8 + 126 FP4), with zero sanitizer errors and unchanged dependencies. The final K-grouped archive contains 8,435 hash-verified files. Paged MQA4320/4320 passes both tools. Dense MQA’s four previously failed packets now pass all48 executions on the final combined wheel; assembled coverage is2304/2304 per tool. Both B300 helpers completed and were archived/released |
| Final-core performance review | All 90 fixed-input case-runs passed; 15 printed-log signals reviewed. A profiler-only large-BF16 signal did not reproduce in six additional sustained-warmup runs (all individual eager/profiler/graph pairs within −3.1% to +3.9%) |
| Variable-length paged performance | Final unmodified current-tree versus dev: all256 cases × six processes pass numerical/input/replay/graph checks; all9,216 raw traces and actual JIT kernels are verified. Every full-operation graph case improves7.19–66.66%. Several logits costs and one discordant full-profiler result remain under investigation |

Outstanding validation as of 2026-09-11 09:14 UTC:

- **Sparse performance is not cleared.** The committed bounded-copy fix passes all161 original cases under both tools and all104 exact-allocation boundary cases under both full-process tools. Its47-case × six-process comparison retains four MXFP4 logits costs of approximately8–12% versus the upstream sparse implementation; sparse is new and has no corresponding dev API. Two private TMA/copy-path experiments each pass208 boundary checks, four original strict checks and282 paired performance runs, but retain material regressions and are not integrated. The simplified OR classifier also passes92 CPU compilations,208 boundary checks, four original strict checks and60 guided performance runs with240 reconstructed traces. It still increases case13 logits/full-call graph latency by14.94%/12.35%, so it is not integrated. A metadata-precomputation prototype has passed all224 actual CPU compilations with zero spills, exact excluded-code audits and independent producer/consumer control-flow review. The original postprocessing failure for half-rendered assertion-line constants is preserved separately from the passing additive byte audit. Compatibility/boundary GPU checks are being prepared; the prototype has no GPU validation yet. All47 cases, including additional performance flags outside the original four targets, remain part of acceptance. Original data and metadata-construction inputs are fixed; the unchanged metadata producer can vary generated schedule ordering, so equal input hashes do not establish identical CTA assignments. This is an explicit measurement limitation, not grounds to dismiss any flag.
- **The final current-tree varlen comparison is complete, with performance issues retained.** All1,536 case-runs,9,216 independently reconstructed traces, original references/20 replays, exact source/wheel checks and actual JIT mapping pass. All146 executed math templates in each arm match explicit zero-spill CPU code. Legacy dev ignores the modern spill environment flag; the baseline evidence comes from actual-code identity, and metadata spill status is excluded. By the ratio of three-arm medians, logits profiler costs exceed5% in cases9/43/193/195, and graph costs exceed5% in9/187/193/195. Case234 is+4.93% by arm medians but+5.21% by median paired percentages; both definitions are retained. The original five residual cases span approximately3.6–7.2% depending on method. Full-operation graphs improve in all256 cases; full profiler improves in255, while case105 is+9.50% with mixed pairs(−17.38%,+15.31%,+13.43%) and an11.41% graph improvement. An unchanged-source repeat of43/104/105/106/234 passes30 runs,180 trace audits and294 cache-identity checks: no logits/full cost exceeds5% in that repeat;105 full profiler improves23.53%, and43/234 flags do not recur. The original outliers remain recorded, and this is not credited as a code fix. A separate legacy required-fence diagnostic passes70 preflight/performance runs,10 original strict packets,420 traces and15 actual-code CPU bindings. Its five historical residual cases add only0.12–0.54% logits profiler cost, so fences alone do not reproduce the earlier5–7% differences. Cross-window comparisons also change physical GPU and allocation history. A completed same-process shared-input diagnostic verifies both module load orders,420 original numerical calls,44 metadata calls,60 isolated timing calls and164 raw traces. Cases9 and193 retain approximately2.8–3.8% profiler/graph latency costs in both load orders;172/187 are near parity, and195 graph cost is1.26%. All120 paired sampled-output checkpoints have equal observed storage addresses and visible extents, including graph outputs; public allocation is not controlled and unsampled profiler outputs are not covered. This narrower five-case window does not replace the full256-case results or establish a code fix. No experimental varlen change is integrated.
- **Integrated spill fixes are verified on the current wheel.** Dense H8/D128 uses the guarded row-index lifetime fix with the original56/224 dynamic register allocation; all48 original packet executions pass strict checks. Four paired throughput medians are+0.42%,+0.63%,+0.42%,−0.58%, with one−3.39% pair retained in the last case. All28 actual generated kernels match the validated fixes, and12 excluded template executable sections remain identical. NVFP4 I8192 preserves the original release-add and synchronization; the current wheel passes the original sentinel/alpha/BF16 two-rank tests. Three sustained full-call latency pairs are+0.106%,−0.144%,−0.142%. Short bursts vary in both directions, so sustained parity is not presented as blanket short-burst parity.

Completed component results are carried only across unchanged executed source dependencies or verified identical kernel text; this is assembled coverage, not a claim that one uninterrupted final `run_tests.sh` invocation has passed. Every original dense/paged/sparse case is accounted for in a disjoint case/tool ledger. pull_requests.title: [NPU] Add AscendC mHC operators for TeleChat4
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

TeleChat4-29B uses four mHC residual streams with `hidden_size=3584`. A Torch decomposition creates many eager launches and intermediate tensors on Ascend NPU. Huawei's `cann-recipes-infer` already provides fused AscendC HcPre and HcPost implementations, but sgl-kernel-npu did not package or expose them and its binding validation did not include 3584.

This PR integrates those official operators into the existing sgl-kernel-npu build and wheel layout. The corresponding SGLang integration is [sgl-project/sglang#33972](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33972).

## Modifications

- Import the official HcPre/HcPost sources from `cann-recipes-infer@3fdb034`, retaining their original copyright and CANN Open Software License Agreement notices.
- Reuse `csrc/attentions/build/build_ascendc_ops.sh` from the main `./build.sh -a kernels` entrypoint.
- Register `torch.ops.npu.hc_pre` and `torch.ops.npu.hc_post`, including Meta implementations.
- Add `hidden_size=3584` beside the existing 4096/7168 binding validation.
- Package the generated vendor tree in the wheel and initialize its custom OPP path on import.
- Add focused correctness tests and a reproducible steady-state benchmark.

The PR does not add a second custom-ops CMake scaffold, compiled artifacts, wheels, cache directories, or a duplicate `ops_common.h`.

## Build and use from source

The build reuses the existing Torch, torch-npu, and CANN installation; it does not reinstall them.

```bash
export SGL_KERNEL_NPU_SRC=/path/to/sgl-kernel-npu

source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
cd "$SGL_KERNEL_NPU_SRC"
./build.sh -a kernels

source "$SGL_KERNEL_NPU_SRC/python/sgl_kernel_npu/sgl_kernel_npu/vendors/aie_ascendc/bin/set_env.bash"
export PYTHONPATH="$SGL_KERNEL_NPU_SRC/python/sgl_kernel_npu:${PYTHONPATH:-}"

python3 - <<'PY'
import torch
import torch_npu
import sgl_kernel_npu

print("NPU available:", torch.npu.is_available())
print("hc_pre:", hasattr(torch.ops.npu, "hc_pre"))
print("hc_post:", hasattr(torch.ops.npu, "hc_post"))
PY
```

For the complete TeleChat4 TP=2 launch commands and `SGLANG_TELECHAT4_MHC_BACKEND=auto|ascendc|triton|torch`, see the dependent SGLang PR.

## Validation

- `bash -n build.sh` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- `./build.sh -a kernels`: passed; the normal wheel contains `libsgl_kernel_npu.so` and the `aie_ascendc` vendor payload.
- `pytest -q tests/python/sgl_kernel_npu/test_mhc.py`: **4 passed** on Ascend 910B3.
- Real NPU HcPre/HcPost correctness checked at 1, 8, and 129 tokens against an HF32-aware Torch reference.
- Meta dispatch accepts 3584 and rejects an unsupported 2048 hidden size.
- Coordinated SGLang tests: **19 passed** (17 mHC dispatch/layout tests and 2 shared-expert top-k tests).
- Native TeleChat4 TP=2 BF16 weight loading and API smoke completed through the AscendC backend.

## Performance

Steady-state Ascend 910B3 latency, 10 warmups and 50 measured iterations:

| Tokens | HcPre | HcPost | Combined |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.0545 ms | 0.0322 ms | 0.0891 ms |
| 16 | 0.0546 ms | 0.0331 ms | 0.0898 ms |
| 128 | 0.0688 ms | 0.0313 ms | 0.0968 ms |
| 512 | 0.1451 ms | 0.0594 ms | 0.2251 ms |
| 1024 | 0.2354 ms | 0.1322 ms | 0.3888 ms |

`msprof op` at 512 tokens measured HcPre at **135.1-136.3 us** (20 AIC + 40 AIV) and HcPost at **48.8-49.3 us** (40 AIV).

The end-to-end 1319-question GSM8K run in the SGLang PR measured **291.248 output token/s** for AscendC, **277.691 token/s** for Triton split-direct, and **107.135 token/s** for Torch fallback under TP=2 BF16, concurrency 16, and NEXTN steps=3.

## Motivation

Add a SYCL implementation for fused mHC post+pre processing on XPU.

The main goal is to improve the small-batch XPU path for mHC by introducing a fused post/pre flow, reducing overhead on token-light workloads, and aligning the implementation with the CUDA-side FMA-style path(https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py#L1070).

## Modifications

- Add the SYCL/XPU `mhc_fused_post_pre` path and `MHCFusedPostPreFmaKernel` for the small-token regime.
- Register the op `mhc_fused_post_pre` and expose it through sgl_kernel. 
- Add unit tests: tests/test_mhc_fused_post_pre.py
- Add benchmark: benchmark/bench_mhc_fused_post_pre.py

## Accuracy

Correctness was validated by comparing the fused path against the unfused reference path:
- reference: `hc_post + mhc_pre`
- target: `mhc_fused_post_pre`

All unit tests passed.

pull_requests.title: perf(dsv4): add MHC token-count prewarm
pull_requests.body: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 MHC pre can hit a large one-time cold cost when a rare token-count bucket first enters the server process. In internal DSV4 profiling runs, the long 20-40s forward stalls aligned with first-seen MHC pre split buckets in sparse mixed/decode tail. This patch moves that first-hit cost into startup warmup so live traffic and benchmark measurement do not pay it at the tail. ## Changes - Add an optional model-level kernel warmup hook in `ModelRunner.kernel_warmup()`, before CUDA graph capture. - Implement the DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm in the DeepSeek V4 model, keeping model-specific logic out of `ModelRunner`. - Gate the hook narrowly to DeepSeek V4 + hybrid SWA + `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1` + `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`. - Infer the warmup range from the normalized `server_args.chunked_prefill_size`; if it is unset or invalid, fall back to `8192`. - Compute one representative token count per MHC pre split bucket under that range, instead of requiring users to manually provide token counts. - Run both attention and FFN `hc_pre` paths on one local DeepSeek V4 decoder layer for each representative token-count bucket. - Expose the MHC prewarm path through the DeepSeek V4 NextN wrapper so the inherited model hook can handle that runtime path as well. ## Notes for reviewers - There is no new user-facing environment variable in the final version. The prewarm range follows the same `chunked_prefill_size` budget used by serving. - With DP attention enabled, `ServerArgs` already normalizes `chunked_prefill_size` by `dp_size`, so `ModelRunner` sees the local per-DP-rank token budget and should not divide it again. - Warming one local decoder layer is enough for this purpose because the MHC pre kernel shape is determined by token count and hidden shape, not by layer-specific weights. ## Accuracy Full GSM8K validation on a B300 DeepSeek V4-Pro DP-attention mixed-chunk setup. The run did not set any `SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM_*` env; the prewarm range was derived from `chunked_prefill_size`. Representative setup: ```bash export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1 export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=2048 export SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH_MOE_A2A=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_NORM=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_JIT_INDEXER_METADATA=1 export SGLANG_OPT_USE_CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_V2=1 export SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0 export SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_FAST_WARMUP=1 python3 -m dynamo.sglang \ --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 6100 \ --trust-remote-code \ --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \ --enable-mixed-chunk \ --context-length 16384 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --expert-parallel-size 8 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --deepep-config '{"normal_dispatch":{"num_sms":96},"normal_combine":{"num_sms":96}}' \ --cuda-graph-max-bs 544 \ --max-running-requests 4352 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.835 \ --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.075 \ --stream-interval 30 \ --tokenizer-worker-num 1 \ --watchdog-timeout 86400 ``` With DP attention, the global `--chunked-prefill-size 16384` is normalized by DP size 8, so each local DP rank sees `max_num_tokens=2048` for this warmup. The worker log confirmed the local prewarm range and representative buckets: ```text Running DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm for max_num_tokens=2048 DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm max_num_tokens=2048 representative token counts: (2048, 1856, 1536, 1344, 1152, 1024, 896, 832, 768, 704, 640, 576, 512, 448, 384, 320, 256, 192, 128, 64) DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm path=attn num_tokens=2048 completed in 28.551s DeepSeek V4 MHC prewarm path=attn num_tokens=64 completed in 28.014s Capture cuda graph end. Time elapsed: 247.96 s. ``` Full GSM8K benchmark output: ```text GSM8K Config: endpoint=http://localhost:8000; num_examples=1319; max_tokens=2048; num_threads=512; num_shots=8; temperature=default; top_p=default; top_k=default Running GSM8K evaluation... Total latency: 131.544 s Score: 0.969 Output throughput: 4405.387 token/s [METRIC] gsm8k_score=0.9687261632341724 labels={"model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro", "eval": "gsm8k"} [METRIC] gsm8k_latency=131.54371510795318 labels={"model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro", "eval": "gsm8k"} {'score:std': np.float64(0.17405684100250698), 'score': np.float64(0.9687261632341724), 'latency': 131.54371510795318, 'output_throughput': 4405.3872092971105} GSM8K evaluation complete ``` ## Benchmark Before: After: Total TPS/GPU from 9266.78 to 9644.40 under conc=2048 on B300 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26182953200](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26182953200) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26182953180](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26182953180)

pull_requests.title: [DeepSeek-V4] Add mhc_fused_post_pre kernel
pull_requests.body: # [DeepSeek-V4] Add fused mHC post/pre kernel ## Motivation This PR optimizes the DeepSeek-V4 mHC path by fusing the boundary between one mHC post step and the next mHC pre step. The approach is adapted from TRTLLM. The main idea is to avoid launching separate kernels for the latency-sensitive decode path: ```text mhc_post -> pre-norm GEMM -> mhc_pre finalization ``` The fused path keeps the existing numerically sensitive `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization stage, but removes the separate post/pre scheduling boundary. For small token batches, a TileLang scalar-FMA kernel computes the following work in one launch: ```text previous hc_post + bf16 residual materialization + pre-norm GEMM partials + RMS square-sum partials ``` For larger token batches, the implementation keeps the existing high-throughput TileLang `mhc_post` + DeepGEMM decomposition. The optimization is guarded by a new env var: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=1 ``` It intentionally depends on the existing TileLang mHC switches: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=1 ``` because the fused implementation directly reuses the TileLang mHC tensor layouts and the `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization kernels. ## Performance Test total_throughput increased by 3.35% ### Performance summary ## Accuracy / Correctness Tests GSM8K score: 0.975 ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` Add: ```python SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE = EnvBool(False) ``` ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py` - Add `mhc_fused_post_pre_fma_tilelang`, a small-token fused TileLang kernel. - Add `mhc_fused_post_pre`, which dispatches: - small batches to the fused FMA kernel; - larger batches to the existing TileLang `mhc_post` + DeepGEMM path. - Preserve the existing `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization stage. - Handle zero-token DP/EP ranks with correctly typed empty tensors. ### `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` - Add fused mHC enable check cached in `__init__`. - Fuse: - cross-layer previous FFN `hc_post` + next attention `hc_pre`; - within-layer attention `hc_post` + FFN `hc_pre`. - Defer the final FFN `hc_post` and close it at model tail. - Cache bf16 RMSNorm weights for the fused path to avoid per-forward casts. ### `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_nextn.py` - Adapt NextN decoder usage to the decoder layer returning deferred fused state. ### `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` - Add coverage for `mhc_fused_post_pre` vs the unfused reference sequence. ## Checklist - [x] Added fused mHC post/pre boundary optimization. - [x] Added env guard `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE`. - [x] Kept the fused path dependent on TileLang mHC pre/post kernels. - [x] Added kernel unit test for fused vs unfused mHC. - [x] Verified operator-level precision. - [x] Verified short deterministic sanity prompts. - [x] Verified GSM8K-200 end-to-end accuracy. - [x] Verified `bench_serving` performance improvement on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26549213709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26549213709) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26549213622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26549213622)

pull_requests.title: Fix DeepSeek V4 NextN fused mHC guard
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek V4 EAGLE speculative decoding uses the NextN draft decoder, which reuses `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` but does not follow the main-model cross-layer fused mHC protocol.

When fused mHC is enabled, the NextN path can incorrectly enter `mhc_fused_post_pre` and hit `post_layer_mix.dtype == torch.float32` assertion failures.

## Modifications

- Track `is_nextn` in `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer`.
- Disable fused mHC post/pre inside the NextN decoder path.
- Enable `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE` by default, while keeping the fused path guarded by TileLang mHC pre/post availability.

## Accuracy Tests

Passed the requested DeepSeek-V4-Flash EAGLE serving validation:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30000 \
  --model /xxx/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name random-ids \
  --num-prompts 128 \
  --random-input-len 32000 \
  --random-output-len 1000 \
  --max-concurrency 4 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --speculative-algo EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4

```

Result: 128 / 128 successful requests. No `AssertionError` or `post_layer_mix` failure observed in server logs.

pull_requests.title: [dsv4] Prewarm MHC prenorm kernel at startup
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

On DeepSeek-V4, the first benchmark run on a fresh server is much slower than later runs (~1016 vs ~1250 tok/s; B300, TP4 / conc 32 / 1k1k / EAGLE). This persists **even though the benchmark already runs a `2×concurrency` warmup** before the timed run: that warmup uses a single fixed-shape input, so it only compiles a few of the MHC prenorm kernel's per-`n_splits` variants; the timed run (random lengths) hits the rest and JIT-compiles them mid-run. A single warmup pass does not fix it — every `n_splits` bucket must be compiled at startup.

Two prior changes are already merged: **#25810** added a model-side prenorm warmup (later reverted — the logic was spread across the model and `ModelRunner`), and **#26238** routed MHC prenorm through the DeepGEMM wrapper and warmed the prenorm GEMM (`tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`) there. However that turned out not to be sufficient, so **#27729** tried to explicitly sweep all `n_splits` buckets of that GEMM — yet the first-run gap remains (see Speed Tests). The reason: `mhc_pre()` runs a second, **TileLang** kernel after the GEMM (`mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm`, specialized per `n_splits`) which is not a DeepGEMM kernel, so DeepGEMM-side warmup never reaches it.

This PR instead warms the actual `mhc_pre()` path at startup. Replaying `mhc_pre()` compiles the TileLang kernel **and**, via the same call, the DeepGEMM GEMM — so it covers what #26238/#27729 warm plus the kernel they miss, superseding them. The second commit removes #26238's now-redundant DeepGEMM prenorm warmup.

## Modifications

- **Prewarm at startup** (`layers/mhc.py`, `environ.py`): on the first non-capturing `mhc_pre()` call, compile the kernel for every `n_splits` bucket over `[1, chunked_prefill_size]` by replaying `mhc_pre()` with the call's real weights; skipped during CUDA graph capture. Gated by `SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM` (default on). One-time cost ~145 s, absorbed into the capture phase.
- **Remove the now-redundant DeepGEMM prenorm warmup** (`deep_gemm_wrapper/`): drop `_TF32HcPrenormWarmupExecutor` and its hook; the runtime GEMM path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Warmup-only change: it compiles the same kernels the runtime already uses, just at startup. No change to model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP4, conc 32, ISL=OSL=1024, EAGLE, `flashinfer_mxfp4`. Standard `2×conc` warmup + `10×conc` timed run, over **two separate server launches** sharing the on-disk JIT cache — `run1` = a fresh server's first run (cold disk), `run2` = warm. Output token throughput (tok/s).

**Does the DeepGEMM-side warmup (#27729) fix it, and is it still needed with this PR?**

| Configuration | run1 (first run) | run2 |
|---|---|---|
| baseline, no #27729 | 1016 | 1250 |
| baseline, + #27729 | 1128 | 1300 |
| **this PR**, no #27729 | **1260** | 1286 |
| this PR, + #27729 | 1269 | 1300 |

#27729 alone lifts the first run +11% but leaves the gap; this PR lifts it **+24% (1016→1260)** and nearly closes the run1↔run2 gap. This PR ± #27729 is within noise (1260 vs 1269) → **#27729 is redundant once this lands.**

**This PR's two commits together (i.e. removing #26238's warmup):**

| Configuration | run1 (first run) | run2 |
|---|---|---|
| this PR, #26238 warmup kept | 1260.3 | 1285.5 |
| this PR, #26238 warmup removed (this branch) | 1260.4 | 1276.0 |

Removing #26238's DeepGEMM prenorm warmup leaves run1 unchanged with a clean startup and **zero lazy kernel compilation during the timed run** — confirming the startup replay covers both the TileLang kernel and the DeepGEMM GEMM.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.

pull_requests.title: [SM120] DeepSeek-V4: DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer +FP4 MoE+ page-split
pull_requests.body:
**Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on
current main the only configuration that starts there is the slow torch fallback — this PR
makes the DeepGEMM and FlashInfer paths work on SM120, cutting decode latency up to 3.4x.

It routes the sparse-MLA indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel, enables batched
sparse-MLA prefill through FlashInfer, and unblocks the DeepGEMM FP4 MoE backend.

## Split out of this PR

Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have
their own PRs:

- #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix)
- #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent)

**This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under
inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once
it lands.

The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on
the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts
for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread
0.01 ms) and roughly 2% of TTFT. Discount the tables by that much, or land #35118 first to
reproduce them as written.

## What is in it

1. **Sparse-MLA indexer on DeepGEMM** — route the indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits
   kernel instead of the eager-torch fallback that scales with batch x context and dominates
   decode. Opt in with `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`.
2. **Batched sparse-MLA prefill** — prefill (q_len > 64) goes through FlashInfer's
   `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`; indexer metadata is chunked at M=4096 (the DeepGEMM
   row cap is SKU-dependent) and built once per batch instead of per layer.
3. **Page-split dirty mask** — `_split_kv_pages_to_64` re-laid out the whole SWA KV pool
   (~105 MB/layer) every decode step; now only the pages this step's top-k references are
   split (CUDA-graph safe, bit-identical).
4. **DeepGEMM FP4 MoE on SM120** — probe the block-scale entry point (DeepGEMM#324) instead
   of hard-disabling DeepGEMM at `sm==120`, plus the contiguous grouped-GEMM prefill path,
   the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant fix, and the swiglu-clamp fallback for TP>=2 shapes.
5. **SM120 kernel fixes** — u64 page-split copy, sparse-prefill head pad removal, TileLang
   `mhc_pre` compile fix, and the paged-MQA metadata kernel now sizes its shared-memory
   request from the device budget instead of a fixed 128 KB.

Non-SM120 architectures are unchanged: every behavioural change is either gated on
`is_sm120_supported()` or is a fix that only engages where the previous code was wrong
(the UE8M0 pow2-scale quant and the shared-memory cap).

## E2E benefit

"main" is marlin MoE + the torch paged-MQA fallback, because that is the only SM120 path on
`14bd315d` that starts: the default (`flashinfer_mxfp4` + TileLang indexer) dies in the
TileLang JIT for `sm_120a` (TileLang ships nvcc 13.3, `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` has CUDA 13.0
headers), and `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` raises `AttributeError: module
'sglang.srt.layers.deep_gemm_wrapper' has no attribute 'get_mn_major_tma_aligned_tensor'`
(SM120 disables `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM` while the runner stays selectable).

Both sides then run identical server args, only the tree differs: TP4, marlin MoE, CUTLASS
FP8, chunked prefill 8192, `--disable-radix-cache`, and no speculative decoding except
where the tables say otherwise. 4x RTX PRO 6000
Blackwell (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe), DeepSeek-V4-Flash, OSL 256, `--warmup-requests 0` so every
measured request is a real prefill. TTFT is a median.

**Single request (BS=1)** — 3 sequential requests, median. TTFT:

| ISL | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 1124 ms | 899 ms | −20% |
| 32K | 4540 ms | 3585 ms | −21% |
| 128K | 20107 ms | 15481 ms | −23% |

TPOT, without and with MTP-2 (EAGLE, 2 steps / 3 draft tokens) on both sides:

| ISL | main | this PR | | main + MTP-2 | this PR + MTP-2 | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 36.1 ms | 10.5 ms | **3.4x** | 13.6 ms | 6.0 ms | 2.3x |
| 32K | 35.8 ms | 10.7 ms | **3.3x** | 12.6 ms | 5.7 ms | 2.2x |
| 128K | 36.1 ms | 11.9 ms | **3.0x** | 13.4 ms | 6.8 ms | 2.0x |

Accepted length is within 0.2 of each other on the two sides at every context length, so the
MTP gain comes from the decode path itself, not from better speculation.

**Concurrent (ISL 8K)** — `--num-prompts BS --max-concurrency BS`:

| BS | TTFT main | TTFT this PR | | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | | output tok/s main | output tok/s this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 3574 ms | 2826 ms | −21% | 42.9 ms | 16.8 ms | 2.6x | 71 | 147 |
| 8 | 5660 ms | 4530 ms | −20% | 51.9 ms | 24.3 ms | 2.1x | 108 | 191 |
| 16 | 10482 ms | 8365 ms | −20% | 71.6 ms | 40.9 ms | 1.8x | 143 | 219 |

TTFT holds at −20% across batch sizes; the decode multiple decays with batch (3.4x at BS1,
1.8x at BS16) because what this PR removes is per-step fixed cost, which amortises as the
batch grows. Speculative decoding amortises it the same way.

GSM8K (50 questions) is 0.980 on main and 0.960 on this PR at 8K — one question apart.

All tables are without prefill context parallelism, which is upstream code this PR does not
touch.

<details>
<summary>Recipes</summary>

Common to both: `--fp8-gemm-backend cutlass --chunked-prefill-size 8192
--max-prefill-tokens 8192 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32`,
plus `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0
SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`.

**Prefill-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --mem-fraction-static 0.85`,
`SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1`.

**Decode-optimised** — `--moe-runner-backend marlin --mem-fraction-static 0.90
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-steps 2
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 3`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1`.

</details>

## Dependencies

- FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (SM120 sparse-MLA kernels) and sglang-kernel 0.4.5 — both are
  what `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` currently ships.
- DeepGEMM at or after deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#324 for the FP4 MoE backend. The
  `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` indexer path additionally needs DeepGEMM's attention host-gates to
  accept SM120 (a 3-line arch gate, not yet upstream in sgl-project/DeepGEMM); without it,
  keep the TileLang indexer default.

## Tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant.py` (9 cases,
registered for CI) covers the fused swiglu-clamp + silu_mul + fp8-quant kernel against a
reference. GSM8K numbers are from `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`.

Reviewed and validated with @ormandj (conflict resolution) and @moxcat (inference-mode
buffer fix, now #35116) on 2x and 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.

Re-validated after the split on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1 (the
pinned version), this tree plus #35116: GSM8K-50 1.000 with `--moe-runner-backend
deep_gemm`, 0.960 with MTP-2; ISL 8K BS1 TTFT 116/88 ms, TPOT 12.8/7.3 ms.

pull_requests.title: [dsv4] Trigger MHC prenorm prewarm at weight-load time with rank sync
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

#27986 made the DSV4 MHC prenorm prewarm trigger lazily inside the first forward that carries tokens — per rank, uncoordinated. On wide-EP disaggregated prefill this is fatal: 0-token EP peers still launch `deep_gemm.fp8_fp4_mega_moe` every layer and wait for the compiling rank inside the kernel's NVLink barrier, which device-traps after 180 s. The 23-bucket burst (one DeepGEMM `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` + one TileLang big-fuse variant per bucket) measures **159–166 s on a cold JIT cache on GB200**, so any >~15 s trigger stagger between ranks blows the budget:

```
DeepGEMM NVLink barrier timeout (180s): rank=2, counter=550, signal=7, target=8, phase=1, sign=0, tag=1
Assertion failed: .../deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/comm/barrier.cuh:76
→ tvm.error.InternalError: CUDA driver error (sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.hpp): 719 (CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED)
```

Reproduces deterministically on GB200 disagg 1p1d dep8-dep16 (8k1k); currently worked around by `SGLANG_DSV4_MHC_PREWARM=0`. Single-node dep4 setups pass only because their triggers happen to align (skew ≪ 180 s) — verified by a synthetic 4-rank repro where a single 200 s host stall reproduces the exact barrier-timeout signature.

## Modifications

- Trigger the same prewarm from the tail of `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights` on every rank — before the memory pool, CUDA-graph capture, and any forward — then `get_tp_group().barrier()` so no rank proceeds while a peer is still compiling, and `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` (this now runs before `init_memory_pool`, so the multi-GB transient prewarm buffers must not skew KV-pool sizing).
- Keep the in-forward trigger as a fallback for entry points that bypass `load_weights` (e.g. kernel unit tests); add prewarm duration + rank-sync logs.
- Remove the orphaned `prewarm_mhc_token_counts/_buckets` pair (added by #25810, removed by #26238, resurrected without a caller by the #25976 merge).

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel/model math changes — the prewarm replays the existing `_mhc_pre_impl` path with dummy inputs at load time (same code the lazy trigger ran). Server responses validated on DSV4-Flash (TP4+DP4+deepep) and DSV4-Pro (disagg dep8/dep16).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A/B on GB200 disagg 2-node dep8 prefill + 4-node dep16 decode — same recipe, container, and base commit; the only difference is this patch:

| | without fix | with fix |
|---|---|---|
| prewarm trigger | 1 rank, mid-serving | all 8 prefill ranks at load (153–173 s, rank sync +0.0 s) |
| NVLink barrier timeouts | 16 (fields match production crash) | **0** |
| sa-bench (isl 8192 / osl 1024, conc 8) | crash, no results | completes, 80/80 requests, 464 tok/s output |

Startup cost is unchanged (~160 s one-shot on a cold JIT cache; ~0 s warm — same as the lazy trigger paid, just moved off the serving path and aligned across ranks).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

pull_requests.title: mhc: portable Triton hc_split_sinkhorn  fallback for non-TileLang bac…
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

`hc_split_sinkhorn` (DeepSeek-V4 mHC) is implemented only in TileLang, which is
CUDA-only. On backends without TileLang (e.g. ROCm/AMD) the module fails to
import, and even the existing torch pre-norm branch
(`SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=false`) still calls the TileLang Sinkhorn
kernel unconditionally — so there is **no portable path** for this op.

This mirrors the situation the Intel XPU work hit in #27783 ("performance kernel
will be provided later"), and it blocks the DeepSeek-V4 mHC path on AMD. This PR
provides that portable kernel and aligns with the AMD roadmap item (#23494) of
rewriting TileLang kernels in Triton for NSA/DSA models.

## Changes

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py`**
  - Make the `import tilelang` optional (a small stub keeps module-level
    decorators/annotations resolvable when TileLang is absent). The module now
    imports on non-CUDA backends.
  - Add a fused Triton `hc_split_sinkhorn` implementation.
  - `hc_split_sinkhorn(...)` now dispatches: tuned TileLang kernel on CUDA when
    available, portable Triton fallback otherwise. **The CUDA path is unchanged**
    (the original kernel is preserved, only renamed to the internal helper).
- **`test/registered/unit/layers/test_mhc_sinkhorn_triton.py`** — registered unit
  test verifying Triton vs a torch reference across token counts, iteration
  counts, and `hc_mult` values, plus the dispatch path.
- **`benchmark/kernels/bench_hc_split_sinkhorn.py`** — before/after microbench.

## Design note (iteration count)

The Sinkhorn loop uses a fixed iteration count (20 for DeepSeek-V4). Validation
against real DeepSeek-V4-Flash weights shows the matrix is **not** doubly-
stochastic at 20 iters (row-sum error ~3–8%) — i.e. the truncated result *is*
the trained target. The fallback therefore reproduces the exact N-iteration
result rather than iterating to convergence, matching the TileLang kernel.

## Correctness

- Matches a pure-torch reference of the TileLang math to ~1e-7 on synthetic
  inputs and on real DeepSeek-V4-Flash `hc_attn`/`hc_ffn` weights.
- `python3 -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/test_mhc_sinkhorn_triton.py`
  → all pass.

## Benchmark (AMD Instinct MI250X; before = vectorized torch, after = Triton)

| tokens | BEFORE torch (ms) | AFTER triton (ms) | speedup |
|-------:|------------------:|------------------:|--------:|
| 1      | 0.973 | 0.089 | 10.9x |
| 128    | 1.000 | 0.090 | 11.1x |
| 2048   | 1.008 | 0.085 | 11.9x |
| 8192   | 1.006 | 0.095 | 10.6x |
| 32768  | 1.130 | 0.142 | 8.0x  |

Reproduce: `python3 benchmark/kernels/bench_hc_split_sinkhorn.py --check`

pull_requests.title: [SM120] Allow fused MHC opt-in with standalone TileLang pre disabled
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

SM120 model post-processing sets `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=False`. `_is_fused_mhc_post_pre_enabled()` also required that flag, so `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=1` had no effect on SM120.

A 60-step C1 trace with the fusion flag set contained, per decode cycle, 86 `mhc_post`, 86 `hc_split_sinkhorn`, and 86 `hc_combine` launches, and zero `mhc_fused_post_pre_fma_tilelang` launches.

`mhc_fused_post_pre` never reads `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE`. It dispatches on its own token-count threshold, taking `mhc_fused_post_pre_fma_tilelang` for small batches and a separate branch for large ones, selecting the GEMM there on `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM`. Both regimes are handled independently of the standalone pre path, so that flag should not gate the fusion opt-in.

## Modifications

- Allow the fused-MHC opt-in to bypass the standalone TileLang-pre flag on SM120.
- Keep standalone TileLang pre disabled on SM120.
- Keep TileLang post required.
- Keep the gate unchanged on other architectures.
- Add a registered CPU unit test covering SM120, non-SM120, fusion opt-in, and TileLang-post policy.

This follows the fused path added in #25976. It does not change the fused kernel or its numerical behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

- Registered CPU unit test (`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_fused_mhc_policy.py`): 3 cases pass.
- Isolated fused-op reference checks: M=1, 2, 8, 32, 384, and 8192 passed.
- GSM8K smoke: 20/20.

## Effect

Hardware: 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q at 300 W, TP2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, FP8 KV, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE, full decode CUDA graphs, EAGLE MTP2.

With `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE` at its SM120 default (off), the non-fused path falls back to `hc_pre_torch_impl`, a torch-level `F.linear`/`rsqrt` implementation. The fusion opt-in replaces it. Median target-verify decode graph:

| | fused off | fused on |
|---|---:|---:|
| Kernel nodes | 3,306 | 2,796 |
| Summed kernel time | 16.230 ms | 14.587 ms |

The 510-node difference is the `hc_pre_torch_impl` fallback. Per-category (fused minus non-fused): gemm_cutlass -767 us (492 -> 407 kernels), other -434 us, gemm_other -320 us (148 -> 63), norm -165 us (130 -> 45), fill -97 us, quant +68 us, sparse_attention +74 us.

Kernel-node counts are structural and do not vary run to run. Throughput is not reported here: the available A/B ran with EAGLE MTP2, whose acceptance rate drifts run to run, and the fused cell spanned 6.9% across five 30 s samples. A non-speculative re-measurement under the settled harness is pending.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit run --files` passed on both changed files.
- [x] Added and registered a CPU unit test under `test/registered/unit/models/`.
- [x] Existing environment variable and interface are unchanged.
- [x] Followed the SGLang code-style guidance.

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Add a HIP/aiter fused `mhc_post` + next-layer `mhc_pre` path for DeepSeek-V4 on
gfx95, dispatched across the attention/MoE boundary alongside the existing TileLang
and Triton fused paths. On MI355X (gfx950) this is a **+0.8%–1.8% output-throughput
win across concurrency 4–64 with accuracy preserved**.

## What changed

- **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`**
  - `try_aiter_fused_mhc_post_pre()`: wraps `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`. The
    aiter kernel self-gates fused-vs-unfused per arch/token-count, so no token
    threshold is duplicated here; import/runtime failures fall back and warn once.
  - `try_mhc_fused_post_pre_boundary()`: aiter → Triton dispatch. The two kernels
    expect opposite fn orientations (Triton transposed, aiter native).
